name: Fiscal conservatism
summary: Fiscal conservatism is a mainly American political position that calls for lower public spending, lower taxes and lower government debt, justified by economic efficiency and by a view of deficits as corrupt; it rejects Keynesian deficit spending and sits close to libertarian limited government. Sources disagree on how far parties claiming it practise it.
scope: Fiscal conservatism as the reference and scholarly sources define it (Citizendium; Savage's chapter): the mainly American position calling for lower public spending, lower taxes and lower government debt. Reagan's 1981 inaugural address is tied only as far as Citizendium names the Reagan era; Goldwater's book and Friedman's Capitalism and Freedom are not named by a defining source found, so their positions answer nothing. It is an economic position, so most statements are null.
